clue.text: Musicians getting tipsy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two nineteenth-century composers named together
second meaning: rhyming slang, where the pair's names rhyme with 'pissed', British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A band starts drinking a little too much before the gig.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it; 'Brahms and Liszt' rhymes with 'pissed', which in Britain means drunk rather than angry.
explanation.definitionFit: The two composers are musicians, and the rhyming-slang phrase is a jokey British expression meaning drunk.

clue.text: A rebate's generating interest

indicators.note: generating means producing something new, so the preceding letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A refund from the taxman is earning money in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The base rate is the central bank's benchmark interest rate, so it is a kind of interest.

clue.text: A form of dislike

parts.note: a version is one form of something

explanation.surface: A particular type of distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong feeling of dislike, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Exploit people like me? Not unknown!

indicators.note: 'not' tells the solver to leave something out of the phrase before it

parts.note: 'my ilk' means people of my kind
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether others take advantage of them, noting they are hardly a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the unknown Y from MY ILK and the remaining letters run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk a situation or person is to exploit them for all they are worth, a verb sense.

clue.text: See 1
Being OK sailing after an upset, life must include golf

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another, setting the order of the chunks
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the short word is read backwards
to include something is to hold it inside, so the letter for golf goes within

parts.note: viability is the capacity to live
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A capsized sailor recovers, with life going on to include a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the short word over; viability, the capacity to survive, stands for 'life' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Navigability is the quality of a waterway or vessel being fit for sailing, a defining-phrase paraphrase.

clue.text: Pull joke on Welshman where bags were carried

parts.note: to lug is to haul or pull
Evan is a typical Welsh first name

explanation.surface: Someone plays a prank on a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here just places the Welshman after the joke in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggage van was the railway carriage that carried passengers' baggage, hence bags carried there.

clue.text: Very wet turf needing study

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Waterlogged grass that ought to be examined.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means soaked through, a plain synonym for very wet.

clue.text: Don't start wasting prize

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: atrophy is the wasting away of a body part

explanation.surface: Advice not to begin throwing away an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or similar object awarded as a prize.

clue.text: The girl is local, Australian originally

definitions.text: The girl is local, Australian originally

indicators.note: originally points at how each word begins, so only opening letters are kept

parts.note: opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A young woman is described as a native, from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a local girl in Australia is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheila is Australian slang for a girl or woman, so the whole description fits.

clue.text: Chemist rejected eggs by the end of long and winding road

indicators.note: rejected suggests being thrown back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
a winding path twists about, so the following letters are jumbled
the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

explanation.surface: A pharmacist turns down eggs after a long and twisting journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chemist' tempts a British reader towards a pharmacist; here it is a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian scientist behind Avogadro's law and number in chemistry.

clue.text: Artist's half-paid blokes pick casual sofa

indicators.note: half applies to each of the following words, keeping just the front portion of each

explanation.surface: A poorly paid painter's assistants choose an informal settee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism is perhaps the most famous artist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Spots some gatecrashers

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters lie within the next word

parts.note: letters four to seven of the word

explanation.surface: Someone notices a few uninvited guests at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' reads as a verb, noticing, but it is a noun: an outbreak of spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots on the skin.

clue.text: Explosion has led to change in the country

indicators.note: changing the letters means putting them into a different order

parts.note: a bang is the sound of an explosion

explanation.surface: A blast has brought about political upheaval in a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh is a country in South Asia, so 'the country' is a broad description.

clue.text: Declare more perverse desire for adulation

indicators.note: to declare is to say out loud, so what follows is judged by sound

parts.note: sicker means more twisted or perverse

explanation.surface: Someone announces a more twisted craving for praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'sicker fancy' gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophancy is fawning flattery, which amounts to heaping adulation on someone powerful.

clue.text: 9, 24, 1 down, 7, 8 and 19 have these tables slowly turning

indicators.note: turning things round mixes them up, so the letters before it are reordered

explanation.surface: A list of cross-references sits beside furniture rotating at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The six answers referred to (SHEILA, PRIMNESS, BASE RATE, SODDEN, TROPHY, SLAP-UP) each have two spoken beats.
explanation.definitionFit: Every one of those listed answers is pronounced in two beats, so they share this property.

clue.text: Paying no attention to gin cocktail circles

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the drink are mixed

parts.note: O and RING are both circles

explanation.surface: Someone overlooks the rings left by a gin drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoring something means deliberately paying it no attention.

clue.text: Dry friend with no mercy

explanation.surface: A deadpan companion who shows no pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting brutally means acting cruelly, without any mercy, so the adverb matches the phrase.

clue.text: Spirit doctor protects poor people infiltrated by mob

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the doctor wraps around the rest
being infiltrated means having something get inside, so the mob goes in

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: poor here means in bad shape, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A doctor shields the needy from an invading gang.
explanation.walkthrough: GANG sits inside the rearranged PEOPLE, and the whole goes between D and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A doppelganger is a ghostly double of a living person in folklore, hence a spirit.

clue.text: Sumptuous clue for friends

parts.note: this is a reverse clue: the answer's final word is the instruction that would turn the first word into the friends

explanation.surface: A lavish puzzle hint aimed at a group of mates.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer itself is the wordplay: SLAP written UP in a down entry gives PALS, so 'slap up' would be a clue for friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, lavishly generous one, so the adjective means sumptuous.

clue.text: In the morning, union discarded uniform for a protective membrane

indicators.note: something discarded is thrown away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Early in the day, a trade union abandons its work clothes in favour of protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The amnion is the membranous sac that encloses and protects an embryo.

clue.text: They comply somehow with a component of the immune system

definitions.text: a component of the immune system

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way of arranging, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Some people go along with part of the body's defences.
explanation.definitionFit: A lymphocyte is a white blood cell, a key part of the body's immune defences.

clue.text: Left The Hague?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the left-hand side of a ship
second meaning: a coastal Dutch city with a harbour, given by example, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone having departed a Dutch city; 'Left' is a side, not a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is the nautical word for the left side, and a harbour town like The Hague is a port.

clue.text: Feel having extracted tooth: at first it hurts

indicators.note: extracting means pulling out, so a letter is taken away
at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A dental patient feels the pain as the tooth comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation of someone in pain, equivalent to saying it hurts.

clue.text: Goliath is never leader in media decorum

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the next word

parts.note: the press is the news media
Goliath is the setter, so 'Goliath is' becomes I'M

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A giant is never a star in the news business.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to themself by pen name, so 'Goliath is' stands for I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Primness is a stiff, formal propriety, a fussy kind of decorum.

clue.text: Starts to bring up money for placement underground

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, which are kept

parts.note: opening letters of the two words
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: A business raising capital to set up in the basement.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial puts a body into the ground, so it is a placement underground.

clue.text: Yep, often hungry, in need of treatment and a donation

indicators.note: something needing treatment is unwell, so the letters must be worked into new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being frequently starving and unwell, and asks for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Before Bonfire Night (5 November) British children traditionally display a stuffed effigy, the guy, and ask passers-by for this.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional children's request for a small gift of money, so it names a donation.
